# YapYap GUI — Implementation Plan

## 1. Locked decisions

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Scope | Full pack **except** W25/W25b Server chrome — "Add a server" rail item shows the `Soon` toast instead |
| Desktop chrome | Custom 32 dp title bar, undecorated, hand-rolled edge-resize, min/max/close buttons per `10-windows.md` §0 |
| Invites | Real QR rendering (qrose, MIT, byte-payload mode) for show-mode; sponsors onboard via paste-base64 path; camera scan deferred to the mobile milestone |
| Connection banner (W18) | Dropped completely |
| Navigation | Ready-made library (see §3), not hand-rolled |
| Distribution | Portable-first (see §2) |

## 2. Distribution & data directory

You can't ship `.jar` files to users — and you don't need to: CMP's `nativeDistributions` already bundles a jlink-ed JRE into every package. The plan:

- **Portable build (primary):** `createDistributable` produces an app folder with bundled runtime; adding a zip step makes the "installer where the user selects the working directory" — unzip anywhere, run the binary, data lives beside the app. Nothing installs into the OS, fully self-contained, matches the decentralized/no-system-footprint ethos.
- **Native installers (kept):** Dmg/Msi/Deb for conventional installs (renamed `YapYap`, vendor/description filled in).
- **Data directory resolution** (first match wins):
  1. `YAPYAP_DATA` env var / `-Dyapyap.dataDir` — multi-instance dev & testing
  2. Packaged app → `<app root>/data` (anchored on the `compose.application.compose.dir` system property CMP sets in distributables — reliable, cwd-independent)
  3. App root not writable (MSI/Deb installs into Program Files / `/usr`) → `~/.yapyap`
  4. Dev `gradlew run` → `./.yapyap` (keeps your existing habit; the leftover `composeApp/.yapyap/tor` stays valid)
- The **effective path is always shown** in Settings → Advanced → Data directory (already spec'd), so there's never a surprise.
- Android: `filesDir/yapyap`; iOS: app-support dir. Multi-instance `.run` configs (instance A/B on the override flag) so you can actually chat between two genesis/joined nodes on one desktop.

## 3. Libraries (ready-made where it's not overkill)

- **Navigation: Voyager** (`cafe.adriel.voyager:voyager-navigator` + transitions) — mature, CMP-first, built-in back stack + transitions, which is exactly what the Medium-class room-list↔chat stack and Compact modal screens need. *Fallback:* if the current Voyager release lags CMP 1.10/Kotlin 2.3.20, use JetBrains' official `org.jetbrains.androidx.navigation:navigation-compose` — decision made at implementation time on compatibility, no design impact.
- **QR: `io.github.alexzhirkevich:qrose`** — KMP QR generation with byte payloads, renders the invite without a camera stack.
- **Serialization: `kotlinx-serialization-json`** + plugin (aligned with `:core`'s version) for `UiPreferences`.
- **`kotlinx-io-core`** — the `Path` type in `OrchestratorFactory`'s signature.
- **Window size classes stay hand-written** — the pack's four classes (600/1024/1440 breakpoints) are custom anyway; a 15-line helper isn't "building by hand", it's just a different constant set than M3's.
- **Material3 stays as a primitive toolbox** (`BasicTextField`, `Slider` state machinery) where its internals can be tuned to the spec; anything with a precise measured look (buttons, switches, rows, menus — the whole `09-component-states.md` matrix) is custom, because M3's defaults would fight the Discord-exact states.
- **Icons: Lucide (ISC)** path data in one `YapIcons` object, 2 dp stroke — explicitly permitted by the pack's legal note; notice file included. **Font: Inter (OFL)** bundled via composeResources, system-sans fallback.

## 4. Architecture

**Platform glue** — a process-level `YapSession` (creates `OrchestratorFactory(dataDir, FULL_CLIENT).create()`, owns the app `CoroutineScope`, `UiPreferencesController`, notification sink; `start()`/`stop()` mapped to `orchestrator.start()/stop()`):
- Desktop: built in `main()`'s `application {}`; `onCloseRequest` → graceful stop.
- Android: `Application` subclass (Manifest edit) so rotation never re-creates it.
- iOS: top-level in `MainViewController`.
- `expect/actual` surface (kept as small as possible): data dir resolution, clipboard, open-folder, desktop notification sink, exit/save-file (recovery-key `.txt` download).

**Packages** (all under `org.yapyap.gui.*` — deliberately clear of the boundary test's core-package list):

```
org.yapyap.gui
  theme/        YapTheme.kt (copied from reference/, verbatim) + YapTheme{} wrapper + motion tokens
  components/   Avatar (deterministic gradient+initials), StatusDot, SoonChip, YapButton, YapTextField,
                YapSwitch, YapSlider, Tooltip, ToastHost, ConfirmDialog, ModalHost, PopoverHost,
                ContextMenu, YapScrollbar, StubPage, StubEmpty
  navigation/   WindowSizeClass helper + Voyager screens (Home, Room, Settings, Friends, Inbox…)
  session/      YapSession, OrchestratorBridge (state→UI mapping), ConnectionBanner=removed
  state/        RoomsController, ChatController (window + grouping + optimistic sends),
                SetupController, SettingsController, ReadStateStore (lastReadAt/pins/mutes/drafts)
  prefs/        UiPreferences + UiPreferencesController (debounced JSON, unknown-key survival)
  capabilities/ Capabilities + LocalCapabilities (real/stub gate per 08-feature-readiness §1)
  copy/         RefusalText mapper, stub toasts, empty-state copy (single source of truth)
  screens/
    boot/ setup/ reset/        S0, S1–S3, S4
    shell/                     S5: rail, room list, chat header, messages, composer, right panel, user panel
    createroom/ settings/      S7, S8/S9 (+ generic Setting renderer + Keybinds table)
    stubs/                     Friends W24, Inbox W28, Pinned W26, Threads W27, Search W20, Voice W29, ProfileEditor W30
    quickswitcher/ W6
  emoji/        Unicode emoji picker (W19): common set, categories, insert-at-caret
  icons/        YapIcons (Lucide path data)
```

**State & practices** (the flexible/mobile-first part):
- All service `StateFlow`s collected via `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()`; screens are stateless, one-way data flow, event lambdas up.
- `ChatController` (Voyager Screen-scoped): `openRoom`/`close` tied to screen lifecycle, `displayItems` → grouped `MessageRow`s (`@Immutable`), optimistic pending rows keyed by local UUID, **deduped/replaced by `messageId`** when the real item lands; sticky-bottom via `derivedStateOf`; anchor-preserving `loadOlder` (keyed `LazyColumn` restores first-visible key + offset after prepend).
- Room list ordering composed per `03-ux-patterns.md` §2.1: local pins → `roomPreview.timestamp` desc → name; re-pulled on every `incomingMessageEvents` and room open. Unread is local (`ReadStateStore`), compared against preview timestamps.
- Setup wizard forms match the real API: Genesis / NewAccount → display name (2–32 chars); AddDevice → no fields, straight to its QR; Recovery → recovery key + bootstrap endpoint (device id, onion address, port). The spec's "device name" field is **dropped** — no API backs it.
- Every destructive/admin flow uses `ConfirmDialog` with type-to-confirm where the docs demand it (remove account, remove last device, reset), refusal values → `RefusalText`, infra throws → toast + preserved input.
- All adaptive behavior per `02-layout-and-adaptive.md`: one collapsing shell (Compact drawer + bottom nav + bottom sheets + long-press menus; Medium swap-stack with back affordance; Expanded overlay right panel; Wide docked panel), `safeDrawing`/`ime` insets, ≥48 dp touch targets, hover-only affordances gated on pointer input.

## 5. Milestones

**M1 — Bring-up.** Theme in place, `YapSession` + entry points on all three targets, custom title bar + edge-resize, `AppRoot` switching on `OrchestratorState` (S0 splash with progress lines), S1 setup wizard (4 paths), S2 recovery-key modal (copy + download + ack-gate), S3 show-mode QR + paste-sponsor flow, S4 reset/failure screens. *Exit:* two desktop instances can run genesis + join via invite, land in the shell.

**M2 — The messaging loop.** S5 shell complete enough to live in: rail (home/Friends-stub/Inbox-stub/pins/invite/settings), room list with all row states, chat header, grouped message list (date + gap dividers, unknown-author rendering), composer (typing signal, byte budget, disabled states, Shift+Enter / IME send), S7 create-room, member list + profile panel, profile popout. *Exit:* you can hold a real conversation between two instances — send, receive, dedupe, retry-failed, type.

**M3 — Discord behaviours & stubs.** Hover toolbar, context menus (message/room/member with Soon actions), quick switcher, settings modal (all sections: Account, Devices, Appearance, Chat, Notifications, Keybinds read-only, Network → Members/Devices/Advanced with the generic `Setting` renderer, Advanced incl. data-dir row + reset), confirm dialogs, toasts, voice-room banner (W29), Pinned/Threads/Search/Inbox/Friends/Profile-editor stubs, emoji picker, keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+K/N/F, Esc, Alt+↑/↓, Ctrl+,, Shift+Esc). *Exit:* full pack minus server chrome; fidelity contract's must-match list verified against `09-component-states.md`.

**M4 — Mobile & polish.** Compact/Medium passes verified (drawer, bottom nav, sheets, long-press, IME), desktop notification sink, window-geometry prefs (1280×800 default restored), tests (below), packaging tasks (portable zip + installers). *Exit:* Android/iOS targets compile and the adaptive shell renders; desktop packaging works end-to-end.

## 6. Tests

- `GuiApiBoundaryTest` stays green (everything lives on the allowed surface; gaps get raised, not bypassed).
- Common unit tests: message grouping (author/time/gap/system boundaries), room-list ordering, refusal→copy mapper coverage, `UiPreferences` round-trip + unknown-key survival, markdown-lite parser, data-dir resolution matrix (JVM).
- One JVM integration-style test: two orchestrators in temp dirs (genesis + sponsor path) with a send/dedupe assertion through the GUI controllers — directly validates the "actually send messages" loop.

## 7. Flagged deviations / API gaps (raised, not worked around)

1. **W18 connection banner** — dropped per your call; A/V-era feature.
2. **Setup "device name" field** — no API; dropped.
3. **File send/download, room rename, message search** — already documented stubs; no new gaps.
4. **`RoomType.UNKNOWN` filtering** — handled per `RoomService.rooms` docs.
5. One question for later, not now: `FanoutReport` renders as advisory only, per `03-ux-patterns.md` §1.6.

If this looks right, the plan is ready for an implementation agent — switch agents (or tell me to hand it over) and I'd start at M1 with the theme, platform glue, and title bar. Happy to adjust any of the calls above (e.g., the data-dir resolution order or the Voyager pick) before you switch.

## [Baret/kotlin-name-generator](https://github.com/Baret/kotlin-name-generator)

# What is Kotlin Name Generator?

Kotlin Name Generator (or KNG for short) aims to provide flexible name generators. It is a library written in Kotlin 
and mainly focused on Kotlin usage. This means you might be able to use it from Java but there are no promises that 
you will have fun.

The idea for this library arose when I needed to generate names for military elements for a game 
([pltcmd, by the way][pltcmd-repo]). These elements are highly hierarchical. For example there might be "Alpha" with its
subordinates "Alpha-1", "Alpha-2" and "Alpha-3". Other elements might need to get "cool names" like "Black Wolves" or
"Phantom Six".

This library offers a simple API to create generators for such names. Let's have a look:

# What it contains and how to use

## The API

You start off with a `WordList`. This is a simple list of Strings that should not be empty and preferably contain unique
values. Except you want some names to have a higher probability to show up or simply repeat specific values.

A `NameGenerator` takes a word list and picks words from it to create `Name`s. That's basically it, but name generators
can be configured in many ways. For example, they can be autoResetting, meaning they produce an endless (repeating) stream
of names. They can pick words randomly or in order. Or they can combine multiple other generators to have sequences like
"Pink flamingos", "Pink pigs", "Blue flamingos", "Blue pigs".

A `Name` is basically a wrapped `String`. In most cases you might need to just get that string, which is possible via its
`asString()` method. But you can even skip the `Name` object by getting `nextAsString()` from a `NameGenerator` 
instead of `next()`.

## [wabbit-corp/kotlin-random-gen](https://github.com/wabbit-corp/kotlin-random-gen)

# kotlin-random-gen

 
 
 
 

`kotlin-random-gen` is a Kotlin Multiplatform property-based data generation library built on
`kotlin-random`.

It provides a declarative `Gen ` DSL, deterministic tape replay, simple shrinking/minimization for
failing values, generated function values through `CoGen`, and low-level bit utilities used by the
replay engine.

## 🚀 Installation

```kotlin
repositories {
    mavenCentral()
}

dependencies {
    implementation("one.wabbit:kotlin-random-gen:2.0.0")
}
```

## 🚀 Usage

```kotlin
import one.wabbit.random.gen.Gen

val userId = Gen.int(1..10_000)
val username = Gen.string(3..12, Gen.printableAsciiChar)
val user = Gen.zip(userId, username).map { (id, name) -> id to name }

Gen.foreach(user, count = 100) { (id, name) ->
    check(id > 0)
    check(name.isNotEmpty())
}
```

...

## Sampling

```kotlin
import kotlin.random.Random
import one.wabbit.random.gen.Gen
import one.wabbit.random.gen.sample

val value = Gen.int(0..99).sample(Random(1234))

check(value != null && value in 0..99)
```

`sample` can return null when a generator rejects a value through `filter`. Use `sampleUnbounded`
when you want to retry until a value is produced.

...

## Replay and Minimization

The sampling interpreter reads bits from a `TapeSeed`. Failed property checks can be minimized and
reported with the minimized tape:

```kotlin
import kotlin.random.Random
import one.wabbit.random.gen.Gen
import one.wabbit.random.gen.foreachMin

Gen.int(0..100).foreachMin(
    random = Random(1),
    iters = 100,
) { value ->
    check(value < 50)
}
```

When minimization succeeds, `MinimizedException` carries the original exception, minimized value,
and replay tape.

...

## Status

This library is useful for internal property tests and deterministic generation workflows. The
high-level `Gen` APIs are the primary surface. Lower-level tape, codec, and bit-sequence utilities
are public support APIs but should be treated as advanced tools.

$ randomname get

## [frikit/krandom](https://github.com/frikit/krandom)
Published: 2018-04-25T00:00:00.000Z

# kRandom

tests + coverage
codecov
Maven Central
License: MIT

kRandom is a Java 21 random and fake-data generation toolkit. The repository is centered on the Java core plus focused integration modules for Jackson, Spring Boot, property-based testing, and Kotlin DSL usage.

...

## What the core currently covers

- Primitive and numeric generators
- Text, lorem-style content, and provider-token templates
- Date/time, timezone, and legacy `Calendar` values
- Network and internet generators
- Locale-aware user/address data plus random supported `Locale` values
- Finance and identifier formats
- Geohash and coordinate-adjacent location data
- File/system/version values
- Selection combinators such as `pick`, `shuffle`, `weighted`, `repeat`, and `unique`
- Reflection-based object graph generation
- Schema-like record generation with `Field` and `Schema`
- Extensible provider lookup with `ProviderHub`

...

## Quick usage

```java
import io.github.frikit.krandom.generator.Generators;

int roll = Generators.ofInt(1, 7).generate();
String name = Generators.ofFullName().generate();
String email = Generators.ofEmail().generate();
String label = Generators.ofProviderTemplate("{firstname}-##").generate();
```

Kotlin consumers can use the same core API directly, or the fixture DSL from
`krandom-kotlin-dsl`:

```kotlin
import io.github.frikit.krandom.dsl.krandom

val user = krandom<User> {
    config { seed(42L) }
    rule("firstName") { "Ada" }
    exclude("password")
}
```

...

## Randomness model

Unseeded generators use the JDK's fast `Random` by default, which is appropriate for fixture and fake-data generation. Use `GeneratorConfig.builder().seed(...)` when output must be reproducible, `GeneratorConfig.builder().random(myRandom)` when a client owns the PRNG instance, `randomFactory(...)` for a fresh custom source per generator, or `secureRandom()` when a consumer explicitly needs a `SecureRandom` source. These source choices are mutually exclusive; `build()` rejects mixed configurations instead of applying call-order precedence.

`Generator.filter(predicate)` is bounded by default and throws if no generated value matches after 10,000 attempts. Use `filter(predicate, maxAttempts)` when a domain-specific predicate is intentionally rare.

...

## Concurrency and determinism

A `Generator` instance is **not thread-safe**: it holds a single mutable PRNG. Sharing one instance across threads is memory-safe (the backing `Random` is synchronized) but interleaves the random sequence — which destroys reproducibility — and serializes callers on the PRNG. The rule for multi-threaded services is **one generator instance per thread**:

```java
// Each thread builds its own generator from a shared, immutable config.
GeneratorConfig config = GeneratorConfig.builder().locale(Locale.US).build();
Generator<String> emails = Generators.threadLocal(() -> Generators.ofEmail(config));
```

`Generators.threadLocal(Supplier)` gives each thread its own instance from the supplied factory. What *is* safe to share:

- **`GeneratorConfig`** has immutable value fields and is safe to share when its caller-owned `Random`, factory, registry, and other extension objects are also used according to their own concurrency contracts. A configured caller-owned `Random` remains shared mutable state.
- **`ProviderHub`** registration is thread-safe; complete all registration before sharing the hub for lookups.
- **`ObjectGenerator` / `ObjectFaker` / `Schema`** are stateful per generation call and must be confined to one thread (one instance per thread).

**Determinism.** A fixed seed reproduces output only under **single-threaded** use of a given instance — concurrent calls race on PRNG call order. For reproducible per-thread data, derive a distinct seed per thread (e.g. `baseSeed ^ threadId`) and build one seeded config per thread. Object generation does not depend on the JVM's unspecified reflection order: fields are populated in a name-sorted order. Seeded output is not guaranteed to be identical across JDK builds, however: values drawn from JDK-supplied data — time-zone IDs from the JDK's tzdata (`ZoneIdGenerator`, `TimezoneGenerator`, zoned date-times), ISO country lists, and locale display names and date formats — follow the running JDK, so pin the JDK version when fixtures must match byte-for-byte across machines.

## [github.com/Anhelmz/namegen](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/Anhelmz/namegen)

# namegen — random adjective–noun names in Go

**namegen** is a tiny open source Go library that builds **random, human-readable names** by combining words from built-in lists. It is useful when you need memorable strings for **development environments**, **internal hostnames**, **test databases**, **staging services**, **container or VM labels**, **demo tenants**, or anywhere you want something easier to say than a UUID.

You describe the shape with a **template string**: each `{adj}` becomes a random adjective and each `{noun}` a random noun. That gives you the familiar “**adjective-noun**” style (similar in spirit to Docker’s random container names), with **hundreds of thousands** of combinations out of the box.

...

## Install

```bash
go get github.com/Anhelmz/namegen
```

Requires **Go 1.24+** (see `go.mod`). That is the lowest version where this module builds as-is: the library uses `math/rand/v2`, and the tests use `testing.B.Loop`.

## Quick start

```go
import "github.com/Anhelmz/namegen"

namegen.GenerateName("{adj}-{noun}")           // e.g. swift-falcon
namegen.GenerateName("{adj}_{noun}")           // e.g. nimble_harbor
namegen.GenerateName("{adj}_{adj}_{noun}")     // two independent adjectives
```

The only public API is **`GenerateName(template string) string`**. Placeholders are replaced in one pass; every `{adj}` and `{noun}` gets its own random pick. Literal text (hyphens, underscores, digits you add yourself) is left as-is.

...

## Vocabulary size and combination counts

The bundled lists currently contain **532** adjectives and **850** nouns. Separators (`-` vs `_`) do not change how many outcomes exist; only the number of placeholders matters.

| Template | Formula | Approximate combinations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{adj}-{noun}` or `{adj}_{noun}` | 532 × 850 | **452,200** |
| `{adj}_{adj}_{noun}` | 532 × 532 × 850 | **240,570,400** |

Each placeholder is an independent draw, so the same adjective can appear twice in `{adj}_{adj}_{noun}`. After you change the word files, multiply your own counts the same way.

# Markdown Text 101 (Chat Formatting: Bold, Italic, Underline)

![](https://support.discord.com/system/photos/7705577612951/Capture.PNG)

[ Buffy](/hc/en-us/profiles/2921470028-Buffy)

- April 23, 2025 17:16

- Updated

Want to inject some flavor into your everyday text chat? You're in luck! Discord uses Markdown, a simple plain text formatting system that'll help you make your sentences stand out. Here's how to do it! Just add a few characters before & after your desired text to change your text! Let’s go over some examples.

**What this article covers:  
**

- [Text Formatting](#h_01GY0DAWJX3CS91G9F1PPJAVBX)

- [Organizational Text Formatting](#h_01GY0DB14X1PFY87CJFFVHFW4T)

  - [Headers](#h_01GY0EQVRRRB2F19HXC2BA30FG)

  - [Subtext](#h_01J2FADV0288YAX4BZ1GNGCHP3)

  - [Masked Links](#h_01H53FJBNB9B5RT9M1M9V1EQ7W)

  - [Lists](#h_01GY0ER08B6V1X2X9X6HT4HTGG)

- [Code Blocks](#h_01GY0DAKGXDEHE263BCAYEGFJA)

- [Block Quotes](#h_01GY0DBAPS5QAB5H7KBXKJZQTB)

# Text Formatting

| *Italics* | \*italics\* **or** \_italics\_ | *Underline italics* | \_\_\*underline italics\*\_\_ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Bold** | \*\*bold\*\* | **Underline bold** | \_\_\*\*underline bold\*\*\_\_ |
| ***Bold Italics*** | \*\*\*bold italics\*\*\* | ***underline bold italics*** | \_\_\*\*\*underline bold italics\*\*\*\_\_ |
| Underline | \_\_underline\_\_ | ~~Strikethrough~~ | \~\~Strikethrough\~\~ |

# Organizational Text Formatting

## Headers

**Note:** Don’t forget to add a space between the leading heading character (`#`, `##`, `###`) and your text!

To create a header you just need to include a specific number of the hash/pound sign character (`#`). Use (`#`) for a big header, (`##`) for a smaller header, or (`###`) for an even smaller header as the first character(s) in a new line to make a header. Here is an example of what each header type looks like.

![headers_example.png](/hc/article_attachments/13850284963735)

![headers_example_two.png](/hc/article_attachments/13850287234583)

## Subtext

Like **Headers**, you can add subtext to any chat message. To do so, add a (` -#  `) before the text you want to appear in the subtext. Don’t forget the space after \# before your message. For example: 

![](/hc/article_attachments/24823996842903)

**![](/hc/article_attachments/24823966227735)**

### Subtext works very similarly to Headers, so the (`-#`) must be at the very beginning of the line in order for it to work.

## Masked links

You can use masked links to make text a clickable or pressable hyperlink. To do so, you need to include the text you want displayed in brackets and then the URL in parentheses. For example:

![link_example.png](/hc/article_attachments/13850326299287)

![link_example_two.png](/hc/article_attachments/13850327352599)

## Lists

**Note:** Don’t forget to add a space between the list bullet (`-`, `*`, `1.`, etc) and your text!

You can create a bulleted list using either (`-`) or (`*)` in the beginning of each line. For example:

![lists_example.png](/hc/article_attachments/13850376284183)

![lists_example_two.png](/hc/article_attachments/13850329913751)

You can also indent your list by adding 2 spaces before (`-`) or (`*`) at the beginning of each line. For example:

![lists_indented_example.png](/hc/article_attachments/13850378577943)

![lists_indented_example_two.png](/hc/article_attachments/13850379795351)

# Code Blocks

You can make your own code blocks by wrapping your text in backticks (`` ` ``). 

![markdown_one_line.png](/hc/article_attachments/13850431807639)

If you want to create a multi-line code block, you can do so by wrapping your text in (```` ``` ````), like this beautifully written haiku.

![markdown_code_block.png](/hc/article_attachments/13850432625431)

# Block Quotes

**Note:** Don’t forget to add a space between the leading \> and your text!

Another option is using block quotes. To use a block quote, you just need to put (`>`) at the beginning of a line of text to create a single block quote. For example:

![block_quotes_single.png](/hc/article_attachments/13850434263575)

![block_quotes_single_example.png](/hc/article_attachments/13850434958743)  
If you want to add multiple lines to a single block quote, just add (`>>>`) before the first line. For example:

![block_quotes_multi.png](/hc/article_attachments/13850437179415)

![block_quotes_multi_example.png](/hc/article_attachments/13850424579479)

Now you're a Discord text markdown expert. Get out there and highlight your statements! 

**Note:** Spoilers is another type of formatting too! Using the syntax \|\| around your text will mark it as a spoiler. Please note, this is negated by a code block. You can learn more about Spoiler Tags [here](https://support.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/360022320632)!

## [mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer](https://github.com/mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer)

# mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer

Markdown renderer for Kotlin Multiplatform Projects (Android, iOS, Desktop), using Compose.

- Stars: 1123
- Forks: 88
- Watchers: 1123
- Open issues: 9
- License: Apache License 2.0
- Homepage: https://mikepenz.github.io/multiplatform-markdown-renderer/
- Default branch: develop
- Created: 2021-10-02T10:09:41Z

## Languages

- Kotlin
- Python

...

## README

 multiplatform-markdown-renderer 

 
 Render Markdown as native Compose UI — one API, every platform.
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 Quickstart •
 Showcase •
 Reference •
 Migration •
 Changelog 
 

| | |
| --- | --- |
| 🧩 **Every platform** | Android, iOS, Desktop (JVM), Web (Wasm / JS) and macOS from one `commonMain` call. |
| ⚡ **Async by default** | `rememberMarkdownState` parses off the composition; `retainState = true` keeps content visible while re-parsing. |
| 🎨 **Material 2 and 3** | Themed defaults from `-m2` / `-m3`; override with `markdownColor()` and `markdownTypography()`. |
| 🧱 **Every element overridable** | `MarkdownComponents` maps each AST node to a `@Composable` you control. |
| 📊 **Full GFM** | Tables, task lists, strikethrough, autolinks and GitHub alerts, out of the box. |
| 📡 **Built for streaming** | `rememberStreamingMarkdownState()` appends chunks and re-parses only the unstable tail. |

## Quickstart

**1 — Add the dependency.** Pick the module matching your Material theme:

```kotlin
dependencies {
    implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer:0.43.0")
    implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer-m3:0.43.0") // or -m2
}
```

**2 — Render.** Import `Markdown` from `com.mikepenz.markdown.m3` (or `.m2`):

```kotlin
import com.mikepenz.markdown.m3.Markdown

Markdown(
    """
    # Hello Markdown

    - Bullet points
    - **Bold** and *italic* text

    Check out this link
    """.trimIndent()
)
```

**3 — Hoist the parse for anything non-trivial.** `rememberMarkdownState` parses asynchronously and
survives recomposition:

```kotlin
val markdownState = rememberMarkdownState(markdown)
Markdown(markdownState)
```

Full configuration — custom components, image loading, syntax highlighting, extended spans — is in
the Reference below.

...

### What's included 🚀

- **Cross-platform Markdown Rendering** - Works on Android, iOS, Desktop, and Web
- **Material Design Integration** - Seamless integration with Material 2 and Material 3 themes
- **Rich Markdown Support** - Renders headings, lists, code blocks, tables, images, and more
- **Syntax Highlighting** - Optional code syntax highlighting for various programming languages
- **Image Loading** - Flexible image loading with Coil2 and Coil3 integration
- **Customization Options** - Extensive customization for colors, typography, components, and more
- **Performance Optimized** - Efficient rendering with lazy loading support for large documents
- **Extended Text Spans** - Support for advanced text styling with extended spans
- **Lightweight** - Minimal dependencies and optimized for performance

...

## Setup

### Using Gradle

Choose the appropriate configuration based on your project type:

 Multiplatform 
 

For multiplatform projects, add these dependencies to your `build.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
dependencies {
    // Core library
    implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer:${version}")

    // Choose ONE of the following based on your Material theme:

    // For Material 2 themed apps
    implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer-m2:${version}")

    // OR for Material 3 themed apps
    implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer-m3:${version}")
}
```

 
 

 JVM (Desktop) 
 

For JVM-only projects, add this dependency:

```kotlin
dependencies {
    implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer-jvm:${version}")
}
```

 
 

 Android 
 

For Android-only projects, add this dependency:

```kotlin
dependencies {
    implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer-android:${version}")
}
```

 
 

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Since version 0.13.0, the core library does not depend on a Material theme. You must include
> either the `-m2` or `-m3` module to get access to the default styling.

...

## Dependencies

This library uses the following key dependencies:

- JetBrains Markdown - Multiplatform Markdown processor
 for parsing markdown content
- Compose Multiplatform - For cross-platform
 UI rendering
- Extended Spans - For advanced text styling (integrated
 as multiplatform)
- Highlights - For code syntax highlighting (optional)

## [MIGRATION.md](https://github.com/mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer/blob/develop/MIGRATION.md)

#### Version 0.44.0

- **Dependency Upgrade**: Kotlin 2.4.0 → 2.4.10
- **Dependency Upgrade**: Android Gradle Plugin 9.2.1 → 9.3.1
- **Dependency Upgrade**: androidx Compose 1.11.3 → 1.11.4 (Compose Multiplatform stays 1.11.1)
- **Dependency Upgrade**: JetBrains `markdown` 0.7.5 → 0.7.9 (required for GFM alert parsing)
- **Dependency Upgrade**: Ktor 3.5.0 → 3.5.2 (affects the coil2 / coil3 network image integrations)
- **New Feature**: GitHub alerts (`> [!NOTE]`, `[!TIP]`, `[!IMPORTANT]`, `[!WARNING]`, `[!CAUTION]`)
 render as styled banners with icon and title.
 - New `alert` component in `MarkdownComponents`, new `MarkdownAlert(...)` render entry point.
 - New models: `MarkdownAlertType`, `MarkdownAlertColors` / `markdownAlertColors(darkTheme)`,
 `MarkdownAlertIcons` / `markdownAlertIcons()` / `DefaultMarkdownAlertIcons`,
 `MarkdownAlertDimens` / `markdownAlertDimens()`, `MarkdownAlertPadding` /
 `markdownAlertPadding()`, plus `MarkdownAlertColorDefaults` and `MarkdownAlertIconDefaults`.
 - New `LocalMarkdownAlertIcons` composition local.
 - Requires the GFM flavour (the default). With a non-GFM flavour alerts stay plain block quotes.
- **Behavior Change**: Block quotes starting with an alert marker now render as an alert banner

- While running: count incrementally from `incomingMessageEvents` (events carry the full display item, so text matching works).

- After a cold start, for rooms never opened: `roomPreview` exposes only the *latest* message, so the pill shows a **dot (count unknown, "at least one")** when that message mentions me; the exact count materializes once the room is opened or events flow. No fabricated numbers.

- Matching is by **display name string** — YapYap has no unique `@handle` (identity is key-based). If two members share a display name, a `@Alice` pill renders for both and both get "mentioned me". # YapYap GUI — Early-Alpha Implementation Plan (Compose Multiplatform)

Status: final, agreed with the product owner (plan-mode discussion, Oct 2026).
Purpose: handoff for an implementation agent. The authoritative specs are the design pack in
`docs/gui/` — this plan records **what to build, in what order, and every decision made on top
of the pack**. Where this plan and the pack disagree, this plan wins (owner-approved deltas).

Primary inputs:
- `docs/gui/README.md` — reading order, fidelity contract, legal constraints
- `docs/gui/01…10` — visual language, layout/adaptive, UX patterns, screens, settings, mapping,

- `docs/gui/reference/YapTheme.kt` — copy into the project verbatim
- `docs/gui-api.md` — the runtime boundary (three orchestrator types + seven services +

## 0. Ground rules

- **`:core` is untouchable.** Zero edits to core sources or build. All GUI code lives in
  `:composeApp` (packages `org.yapyap.gui.*` — outside the boundary test's core-package list).

- Root-level changes allowed: `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, root `build.gradle.kts` plugin
  registration, `composeApp/build.gradle.kts`, `composeApp` sources, `.run` configs,
  Android `AndroidManifest.xml` (Application class), packaging config.
- Fidelity contract per `docs/gui/README.md` (must-match list) and
  `09-component-states.md` (state matrix) are non-negotiable.
- Stubs follow `03-ux-patterns.md` §8: real chrome, placeholder content, `Soon` chip/action,

## 1. Locked decisions (owner-approved)

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Scope | Full pack **except** W25/W25b (Server view & Server settings). "Add a server" rail item shows the `Soon` toast instead. |

- Android: `Application` subclass (Manifest edit) so rotation never recreates it.
- iOS: top-level `remember` in `MainViewController`.

`expect/actual` surface kept minimal: data-dir resolution, clipboard, open-folder,

  identity/     DeviceNames (§6), avatar/banner generation
  emoji/        Unicode emoji picker + shared name table
  icons/        YapIcons (Lucide path data)
  screens/
    boot/ setup/ reset/          S0, S1–S3, S4
    shell/                       S5: rail, room list, chat header, messages, composer,

    stubs/                       Friends W24, Inbox W28, Pinned W26, Threads W27,

```

### State & Compose practices
- Service `StateFlow`s collected with `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()`; screens stateless,
  one-way data flow; `@Immutable` GUI models (`RoomListItem`, grouped `MessageRow`).
- `ChatController` (screen-scoped): `openRoom`/`close` tied to screen lifecycle;
  `displayItems` → grouped rows; optimistic pending rows keyed by local UUID, **deduped and

- Room list ordering per `03-ux-patterns.md` §2.1: local pins → `roomPreview.timestamp`
  desc → name; re-pull on every `incomingMessageEvents` and on room open.
- Read state is local (`ReadStateStore`) — per-device, no fake server semantics.
- Every destructive/admin flow uses `ConfirmDialog` (type-to-confirm where docs demand:
  remove account, remove last device, reset); refusal values → `RefusalText`; infra throws →
  toast + preserved input.
- Adaptive: ONE collapsing shell per `02-layout-and-adaptive.md` (Compact drawer + bottom

  overlay right panel; Wide docked panel). `safeDrawing`/`ime` insets, ≥48 dp touch targets,
  hover-only affordances gated on pointer input.
- Message content rendering is one exhaustive `when` over `MessageDisplayItem` (seam per
  `06-yapyap-mapping.md` §5).

- `kotlinx-io-core` (the `Path` in `OrchestratorFactory`'s signature)
- `kotlinx-serialization-json` + serialization plugin (UiPreferences; version-aligned with core)
- `io.github.alexzhirkevich:qrose` (QR generation, byte payloads)
- `cafe.adriel.voyager:voyager-navigator` (+ `voyager-transitions`) — or JB navigation-compose fallback

- `kotlinx-datetime` (timezone/DST-correct `<t:>` formatting; aligns with `kotlin.time.Instant`)

Kotlin 2.4 metadata; we are on CMP 1.10.3 / Kotlin 2.3.20 (+1 forward metadata compat should
hold). If resolution fails: either bump CMP in the catalog (GUI-side decision — core has no
Compose dependency) or pin an older renderer release aligned to 1.10. Voyager likewise.

## 4. Distribution & dev workflow

- Packaging: `nativeDistributions` kept (Dmg/Msi/Deb, packageName "YapYap", vendor/description
  filled in) + portable zip task over `createDistributable`.
- `.run` configs: "Desktop app", "Desktop app (instance B)" using `-Dyapyap.dataDir`
  overrides so two nodes (genesis + join) can chat on one desktop.
- Data-dir resolution per §1; always render the effective path in Settings → Advanced.

## 5. Markdown — Discord dialect on a ready-made parser

Parser/renderer: `multiplatform-markdown-renderer` (async `rememberMarkdownState`,
cache by content hash so message rows parse once per text change). Everything standard
(bold/italic/combinations, strikethrough via GFM, lists incl. 2-space indentation, autolinks,
masked links, inline code, escapes, fenced code, headers, quotes) = library behavior styled
to `YapColors`/`YapType`.

Our layer in `org.yapyap.gui.markdown`:

1. **`DiscordMarkdownTransformer`** (pre-parser string pass, **code-aware**: mask
   `` ` ``-spans and ``` ``` ```-blocks first, transform, restore — spoilers/mentions are
   negated inside code, per Discord):
   - `__underline__` → underline sentinels (**CommonMark would read `__` as bold** — must rewrite)
   - `||spoilers||` → spoiler sentinels
   - `<t:unixSeconds:style>` → timestamp sentinels
   - `>>>` (quote-to-end) → expand to per-line `>`
   - `-# subtext` → `######` (renderer maps h6 → subtext style)
   - `:shortcodes:` → emoji chars (shared table with the picker)
   - Sentinel chars are private-use-area; **strip unknown PUA from input first** so nobody can forge them
2. **Custom components/spans** (MarkdownComponents overrides): spoiler (tap-to-reveal +
   respects "Show spoiler content" pref), timestamp chip (all styles `t T d D f F R`; `R`
   relative on a refresh tick), mention pill (§7), code blocks on `#242429` inset with
   language label, quote accent bars, Discord header sizes (h1 big / h2 / h3 small),
   link color + underline pref.
3. Room-list previews and notification snippets render **stripped plain text** with mention
   ids substituted to display names. `Copy text` copies raw source (ids included) — matches Discord.

Supported grammar (from the live support article + Discord timestamp syntax):

| Category | Syntax |
|---|---|
| Emphasis | `**bold**`, `*italic*` / `_italic_`, `***bold italic***`, `__underline__`, `~~strikethrough~~`, all `__**…**__` combinations, `\` escapes |
| Structure | `# ## ###` headers, `-#` subtext, `-`/`*`/`1.` lists + 2-space indent, `>` / `>>>` block quotes (nested) |
| Code | `` `inline` `` + ``` ``` ``` fenced blocks with language label; syntax highlighting optional M4 stretch |
| Links | bare-URL autolinks, `[masked links](url)` |
| Extras | `\|\|spoilers\|\|`, `<t:unix:style>` dates, `:shortcodes:` |
| Mentions/channels | `@<AccountId>` / `@everyone` / `#<RoomId>` — §7 |

## 6. Device names

`DeviceNames.from(peerId)` → `"Amber Falcon"` style: curated versioned adjective × noun
word lists (~500k combinations; collisions irrelevant at network scale), deterministic via
SHA-256 of `PeerId.id` → two stable list indices. Golden tests pin output so names never
silently change between releases. **Every device row always shows the full `PeerId`**
(`bodyXs`, muted, copyable) beside the prominent name — no collision-detection logic.
Same deterministic-hash utility powers generated avatars/banners. Display-only sugar;
identity stays `DeviceView` (type icon + last seen alongside).

## 7. Mentions — id-based, fully GUI-side

Wire format in plain message text (backend never interprets it):

| Token | Resolves to | Renders |
|---|---|---|
| `@` + 64-hex (`AccountId.id` = SHA-256 hex of account signing key — rigid token, names can contain anything) | `identity.account(id)` live at composition time | mention pill (`#5865f2` @ 24 %, `#cdd7ff` text) with the account's display name; unknown → muted "Unknown user" pill |
| `@everyone` + boundary | keyword | `@everyone` pill (group ping; `@here`/roles out — no role model) |
| `#` + UUID (`RoomId.value`) | room list / `rooms.room()` | clickable room ref; opens the room; unknown → muted plain text |

- **Composer**: `@` opens member autocomplete, `#` opens room picker; both insert the id
  token + trailing space. Users never type hex. Freeform `@alice` renders as plain text.
- **Mention-of-me** = id equality with `localAccount` (+ `@everyone`), minus self-authored
  messages — deterministic, no name-collision ambiguity.
- **Consumers**: message-row highlight (`#f8a300` @ 8 % fill + 2 px left bar per
  `03-ux-patterns.md` §1.2); red mention pill on room rows (`#da3e44`, white count) cleared
  on open/mark-read; desktop notification **only when window unfocused** (respects the
  "Notify when the window is focused" toggle); bundled notification sound (respecting its
  toggle) — real on desktop; taskbar/dock badge where supported (best-effort); NEW-messages
  divider (red bar + label) + jump-to-present integration.
- **Counting mechanics** (honest): incremental from `incomingMessageEvents` while running;
  recomputed from the loaded window vs `lastReadAt` on room open; after cold start, for
  never-opened rooms the preview exposes only the latest message → render a **dot (count
  unknown)** when that message mentions me. Never fabricate numbers.
- **Mobile push**: deferred — a real pipeline needs the backend to let a woken app fetch and
  decrypt the actual message (E2EE payloads can't ride a push). The `NotificationSink` seam
  is where it plugs in.
- **Settings impact**: mention rows in Notifications move from `Soon`-chipped to real;
  sound real on desktop; push stays the stub row.
- A protocol-level mention annotation (badges/notifications server-side semantics) remains a
  possible future backend feature; `MentionMatcher` is the seam where it lands.

+ hand-rolled edge-resize + window prefs; dependency spike (markdown renderer + Voyager

rendering, composer with typing signal + byte budget + disabled states + Shift+Enter/IME,

`Ctrl/Cmd+,`, `Shift+Esc`).
*Exit:* full pack minus server chrome; must-match fidelity list verified against
`09-component-states.md`.

**M4 — Mobile & polish.**
Compact/Medium passes (drawer, bottom nav, sheets, long-press, IME handling); desktop

## 9. Tests
